title: Ramayana Posts Record Second Friday, Second-Biggest Ever for a Hindi Film
excerpt: Nitesh Tiwari's epic collected about Rs 47 crore nett across India on its second Friday — a record for the day — while its Hindi version's Rs 36 crore ranked second only to Dhurandhar: The Revenge.
body:
• Ramayana: Part One collected approximately Rs 47 crore nett across India on its second Friday, the highest second-Friday figure recorded at the Indian box office, according to Pinkvilla's trade estimates.
  • The Hindi version netted Rs 36 crore on the day, the second-biggest second Friday for a Hindi film, behind Dhurandhar: The Revenge at Rs 36.50 crore.
  • The Hindi total reached about Rs 465 crore nett by Pinkvilla's count (Rs 461 crore by Box Office India's), after a drop of just 12% from the previous day.
  • All figures are trade estimates compiled by the trackers, not certified collections.

Ramayana: Part One, the Hindi-language epic directed by Nitesh Tiwari and starring Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi, has carried its opening-week momentum into a second week, recording the biggest second Friday in Indian box office history, according to Pinkvilla, while falling just short of the Hindi record.

Across all languages in India, the film collected approximately Rs 47 crore nett on its second Friday — Rs 36 crore from the Hindi version and Rs 11 crore from the dubbed versions — which Pinkvilla ranked as the highest second-Friday haul at the Indian box office. On the gross side, Pinkvilla's daily-records tracker put the day at Rs 56.25 crore, ahead of the previous best of Rs 49.50 crore held by Baahubali: The Conclusion.

Second in Hindi, by Rs 50 lakh

In Hindi alone, the Rs 36 crore nett second Friday is the second-biggest ever, behind only Dhurandhar: The Revenge at Rs 36.50 crore, Pinkvilla's chart shows. Box Office India called the hold "outstanding," noting the 12% drop from the previous day came without the ticket-price increase that normally supports a second-Friday hold, and put the Hindi total at Rs 461 crore nett after nine days, with the dubbed versions adding Rs 128 crore nett.

Trackers differ slightly in their tallies, as they do on most big releases. Sacnilk put the all-language second Friday at about Rs 48 crore nett across five languages, overtaking Dhurandhar 2's benchmark of about Rs 42 crore, and the Hindi figure at about Rs 36.50 crore. All three trackers agree on the ranking itself: first in India overall, second in Hindi.

What the hold signals

A second-Friday drop of 12% is the pattern of a film being carried by word of mouth rather than opening-weekend curiosity. Pinkvilla noted the film has taken the single-day records from Monday onward through its run. The test now is whether the hold consolidates across the second Saturday and Sunday, which would put the records for those days in play as well.

Ramayana: Part One is the first instalment of Tiwari's two-part telling of the epic, with Kapoor as Ram, Yash as Ravana and Sai Pallavi as Sita. The box office figures in this report are the trackers' trade estimates, compiled from commercial parameters and market trends; Pinkvilla states they are not finalised or certified collections.
